correctness.rationale: Frozen RESULT.md derives two-year monodromy M_2=(J D_m G_0)^2, with nonnegative transformed 2-by-2 T. Its Perron root R(m)=[sm(a+b)+sqrt(s^2(a-b)^2m^2+4ab(1-m)^2)]/2 applies to all a>b>0, 0<s<=1, 0<=m<=1 with positive starts at reducible endpoints. Explicit R''(m)=s²(a-b)²(2sqrt(ab))²/[2(sqrt(s²(a-b)²m²+4ab(1-m)²))³]>0 proves only endpoints maximize: m=1 if s>sqrt(b/a), m=0 if less, endpoints tie at equality. R'(0)=s(a+b)/2-sqrt(ab) gives distinct infinitesimal threshold 2sqrt(ab)/(a+b), so in nonempty intermediate interval complete migration is best while every sufficiently small migration is worse. Exact witness a=4,b=1/5,s=3/10 has R(0)=2/sqrt5, R(1/10)=87/100, R(1)=6/5 and unique R(m)=1 at (85+5sqrt(1745))/364. Independently recalculated T trace/determinant and witness numerically (m_c~0.80732413665, R(m_c)=1). Strict convexity proves interior cannot be global maximum, not merely from sampled m. No stochastic extinction claim.
